To: support@clockpoint.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: kevin.mutua@tausifreight.example
Subject: Re: [CP-48213] Overtime coding issue on night shifts

Dear Faith,

Please find the details below. I have copied Kevin Mutua, our payroll officer, who will test any fix or workaround you suggest.

1. Terminals and firmware: The four BX-300 terminals at Embakasi auto-updated from 4.1.8 to 4.2.1 on the night of 27 October. Our two Mombasa Road terminals remain on 4.1.8; the day shift there is unaffected.

2. Shift template: NIGHT-8, scheduled 22:00–06:00 at Embakasi.

3. Example: Staff ID T-0417 clocked in at 21:54 on 30 October and out at 06:07 on 31 October. All times are Nairobi time (EAT).
The export showed:
- 30 October: 2.1 hours REG
- 31 October: 6.1 hours OT15

The expected result is 8.0 hours REG plus 0.2 hours OT15. Payroll rounds durations to the nearest tenth of an hour: the total of 8 hours 13 minutes rounds to 8.2 hours, with the 13 minutes outside the scheduled shift coded OT15.

4. Export profile: Payroll CSV v2.

5. Timing: Kevin first noticed the issue on 5 November while reviewing draft October overtime. It appears to affect shifts from about 28 October, splitting shifts across midnight into two lines and coding the after-midnight portion as OT15 rather than REG.

This affects 38 night-shift staff and overstated draft October overtime by approximately KES 212,000. Kevin has held the overtime lines and manually corrected them against raw punches, but this is not sustainable each month.

The 4.2.1 release notes promised improved midnight rollover handling; our experience has been the opposite. We need a fix or clear workaround before payroll cut-off on 20 November. Please confirm your next steps and expected timing.

Can Brian Ochieng, our IT colleague who manages the terminals, safely roll Embakasi back to 4.1.8 without losing punch data? Please confirm any backup requirements and the supported rollback procedure before he proceeds.

Regards,
Njeri Mwangi
HR Manager, Tausi Freight
